children: By Chibuike Oguh and Amanda Cooper
Global stocks rallied on Wednesday after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress in the
, providing greater political clarity and reducing the uncertainty that has weighed on markets.

In a major setback to President Donald Trump, Democrats scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations. The breadth of the party's success was underscored by gains in districts long considered safely conservative, highlighting a political shift that may have caught some investors off guard.

On Wall Street, all three main indexes were trading higher with communication services, consumer discretionary and technology stocks driving gains. Energy shares were the biggest losers on the day with crude prices down 2% as Trump acknowledged that the
had played a role in his party's sweeping defeat.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average
rose 2.05%, the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
was up 1.72%, and the Nasdaq Composite
gained 2.46%.

"Markets hate uncertainty and even though a lot of what the result was had been priced in ahead of time, getting confirmation of that last night brings certainty to markets," said Clayton Allison, portfolio manager at Prime Capital Financial. "Now this brings questions as to what actually gets done in Washington over the next two years. But the markets love to see that there is a resolution to a catalyst event."
Opinion polls have shown Democratic voters favouring more control over AI, and investors expect the Democratic-controlled Congress to apply more scrutiny to the sector.
The MSCI All-World index
EURONEXT:IACWI
was up 1.3%, while Europe's STOXX 600
, which has acted as a hedge against AI-related risks, jumped 1.84% to two-month highs.
AI stocks in Asia initially led a decline in equity markets before finishing higher overnight.  MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) rose 0.33%.

The AI boom has helped propel global markets in recent years, driven by heavy spending from tech giants racing to build data centers and expand computing capacity. That has made investors acutely sensitive to anything that could derail the technology's rapid expansion.
Advanced Micro Devices
rose 1% in early trading after the US chipmaker forecast faster growth through 2027, reassuring investors that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.
SAFE HAVEN BID
Treasuries rallied as investors expect gridlock in Washington to cut government spending, with AI regulation also possibly slowing growth and reducing the need for rate hikes.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note
was down 0.44 basis point on the day at 4.95%, having fallen as much as 6 bps to a low of 4.89% overnight, which, in turn, weighed on the dollar
The broadly weaker dollar left the euro
up 0.40% at $1.1234 and the pound up 0.41% at $1.3469
The yen
and the Swiss franc
— both safe-haven currencies — also notched gains. The Swiss franc
was up 0.35% against the dollar at 0.818 francs. The Japanese yen
edged 0.07% higher to 158.61.
Brent crude oil futures

were down 2.2% on the day at $101.27 a barrel as investors weighed Washington's next move in talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin
gained 3.49% to $80,553.92. Ethereum
Spot gold
rose 2.72% to $4,036.49 an ounce.
